title: Unified Ops Protocol: Access, Change, Data & Vendor Lifecycle
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document provides a unified, company-wide protocol for operational controls that span access and permissions, change management, data handling, procurement & expenses, vendor lifecycle, and travel rules. It consolidates commonly used templates, decision thresholds, and step-by-step flows so teams can follow consistent processes and auditors can validate controls.

Goals
- Reduce approval friction for low-risk changes while preserving strong controls for sensitive assets.
- Provide clear, auditable trails for procurement and vendor decisions.
- Standardize role-based access tiers and self-service patterns.
- Ensure data classification drives handling and retention decisions.

Scope
Applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party vendors interacting with Redwood systems or representing Redwood in procurement or travel. Exceptions require documented risk sign-off from Finance-Legal and Security.

Owner & Escalation
- Policy owner: Finance & Legal (primary), Security (co-owner for data/access sections)
- Day-to-day operations: Shared Services (procurement/expenses), IT Ops (access provisioning), SRE (change management for production systems)
- Escalation: Director, Finance -> VP Ops -> Legal Counsel for contract exceptions

1) Access & Permissions
Purpose: Ensure least-privilege access with tiered approvals and automated reviews.

Roles and tiers
- Tier 0 (Public): Documentation, non-sensitive marketing assets. Justified by system owner.
- Tier 1 (Internal): Internal dashboards, code repos without prod secrets. Auto-approval by manager for onboarding. Quarterly review.
- Tier 2 (Restricted): Production systems metadata, customer metadata (non-PII). Requires manager + system owner approval. Monthly review and IAM recertification.
- Tier 3 (Sensitive): PII, Secrets, KMS/HSM access, audit logs. Requires manager + system owner + security approver. 30-day emergency token TTL.

Provisioning workflow (standard)
1. User submits access request using the Access Portal (access.redwood.internal). Include justification, requested tier, and duration.
2. Manager approves or rejects within 48 hours. If no response, request escalates to manager's manager.
3. System owner validates least-privilege and either approves or requests scope reduction.
4. Automation provisions access and records grant ID in IAM audit log.
5. Scheduled recertification emails sent based on tier cadence.

Emergency access (break-glass)
- Submit Break-Glass request via PagerDuty incident with ticket link. Security will issue a time-limited token (max 24 hours) after documented justification. Post-incident, owner must run a retrospective and revoke or rationalize further.

Access review matrix (summary table)
| Asset class | Example services | Approval chain | Review cadence | Retention of evidence |
|-------------|------------------|----------------|----------------|----------------------|
| Public | Marketing site | Manager | Annual | 1 year |
| Internal | Internal dashboards | Manager | Quarterly | 1 year |
| Restricted | Prod read-only | Manager + Owner | Monthly | 3 years |
| Sensitive | KMS, DB write | Manager + Owner + Security | Monthly | 7 years |

2) Change Management
Purpose: Ensure predictable rollout of changes to infra, runtime, and customer-facing systems.

Change classes
- Standard (low risk): Pre-authorized routine ops (e.g., adding capacity, package updates with green tests). No CAB needed.
- Minor: Non-customer-impacting changes requiring owner approval and automated canary.
- Major: Customer-facing or schema/DB migrations, requires CAB review and rollout plan.
- Emergency: Mitigation of active incidents; follow post-facto CAB review.

Change process (major change checklist)
1. Author prepares Change Request (CR) in Change Tracker including impact analysis, rollback plan, test plan, and monitoring playbook.
2. Submit CR at least 72 hours before planned window.
3. Engineering owner coordinates a pre-CAB review with SRE and Security.
4. CAB meeting: Approvers = Service Owner, SRE Lead, Prod Support, Security Rep, and Product Owner. Decision documented.
5. If approved: schedule in maintenance window, assign runbook author and observers.
6. Execute with live monitoring and rollback guardrails. Capture incident metrics.
7. Post-change review within 48 hours summarizing variance from plan and action items.

Rollback criteria (example)
- Error rate > 3x baseline for 10 consecutive minutes OR
- p95 latency exceeds SLO by 2x for 5 minutes OR
- Any customer-facing data loss or corruption detected.

3) Data Management and Classification
Policy summary
- Data is classified at creation: Public, Internal, Restricted, Sensitive. Classification governs storage, transit encryption, and retention.
- Sensitive data requires encryption at rest (customer-managed KMS for Private deployments) and strict access controls.

Data handling rules (quick reference)
- Transit: TLS 1.2+ required for all external traffic; internal calls must use mTLS.
- At rest: AES-256 or better. DB backups with separate key lifecycle.
- Logging: PII must be redacted before ingestion into observability systems.
- Retention: Default retention is 3 years for Restricted, 7 years for Sensitive unless legal hold applies.

Data classification decision tree (example)
1. Does the data identify an individual? -> Yes => Sensitive or Restricted.
2. Is it covered by contract/regulation (GDPR/CCPA/HIPAA)? -> Yes => Sensitive.
3. Is it telemetry or aggregated metrics? -> Likely Internal.

4) Procurement & Expense Controls
Procurement thresholds and required approvals
- < $5k: Team lead approval; use corporate P-card where available. Purchase must attach quote and purpose.
- $5k–$50k: Procurement ticket + Finance approval; at least one competitive quote preferred.
- $50k–$250k: Procurement + Finance + Legal review for contracts. Vendor security questionnaire required.
- > $250k: Leadership approval (Director+) and VP-level review; full procurement RFP recommended.

Expense categories and documentation
- Travel: itemized receipts required; per-diem caps applied by region.
- Software subscriptions: submit seat count and renewal terms 30 days before expiry.
- Capital vs. expense: Finance will classify per capitalization policy and notify requestor.

Vendor security & procurement checklist (minimum)
1. Completed Vendor Intake Form (VIF) with scope and contact information.
2. Security questionnaire or SIG profile.
3. Proof of insurance & SOC2 or equivalent where applicable.
4. Contract with standard Redwood terms; deviations require Legal sign-off.
5. Procurement entry in vendor registry and assigned owner.

Template: Procurement request fields (for portal)
- Project name
- Business owner
- Estimated annual spend
- SOW/contract link
- Data access required (Yes/No; if yes, classify data)
- Security assessment result link

5) Vendor Lifecycle Management
Stages: Evaluate -> Onboard -> Monitor -> Offboard

Evaluate (selection)
- Use standard RFP template for >$50k. Score vendors on security, cost, SLAs, and integration complexity.
- Shortlist 2–3 vendors when practical.

Onboard
- Assign internal vendor owner and designate integration engineer.
- Configure least-privilege access in a dedicated service account; no shared credentials.
- Register vendor in Vendor Registry with onboarding artifacts.

Monitor
- Quarterly risk review for strategic vendors; annual for tactical vendors.
- Track SLA performance, security posture changes, and cost trends.

Offboard
- Revoke credentials, certificates, and application tokens.
- Confirm data deletion/return per contract.
- Perform final security scan and closure checklist.

6) Travel & Expenses (key rules)
- Business class travel permitted for flights >8hrs economy alternative required if <8hrs. Exceptions require Director approval.
- Hotel standard: business or mid-range corporate rates; upgrades require justification.
- Per-diem: set by region (refer to Travel Rates appendix). Receipts required for expense reports > $25.
- International travel: complete pre-approval and security briefing if traveling to high-risk countries.

Expense submission workflow
1. Submit expenses with receipts within 15 calendar days of trip.
2. Manager approves within 7 days or escalates.
3. Finance processes reimbursement within standard payroll cycle.
4. Excess or unusual expenses flagged for audit.

Templates and attachments
- Access request template (fields)
- Change Request (CR) template and checklist
- Vendor Intake Form (VIF) sample
- Procurement request form JSON example:
{
  \"project\": \"Example Integration\",
  \"owner\": \"team@example.redwood\",
  \"estimated_annual\": \"18000\",
  \"data_access_required\": \"Yes\",
  \"classification\": \"Restricted\"
}

Audit and Reporting
- All approvals and artifacts must be retained in the central Governance bucket with indices for at least the retention period specified by the control (see Access review matrix).
- Monthly operational dashboard: open change requests, outstanding procurement approvals, and active emergency access tokens.
- Annual independent audit: Finance & Legal coordinate with Security to validate vendor and access controls.

Exceptions and re-evaluation
- Exceptions follow an Exception Request process: submit business justification, compensating controls, and a time-bound approval (max 12 months). Legal & Security must co-sign.
- Policy review cadence: Every 12 months or after a major incident.
